newsitem.title: PERU: Malaysian minister meets Fujimori over Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian minister meets Fujimori over Peru crisis.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi met on Thursday with Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori to discuss the 9-day-old hostage crisis in Lima.
Malaysia's ambassador to Peru, Ahmad Mokhtar, was one of 103 VIP hostages still being held at the Japanese ambassador's residence by rebels belonging to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
Government Palace officials said the meeting, which was also attended by the goverment's designated mediator, Education Minister Domingo Palermo Cabrejos, lasted just over an hour.

"During the interview, the president informed him (Abdullah Ahmad) of the situation going on in the residence of the Japanese ambassador in Lima," state news agency Andina said. Neither the agency nor officials gave further details of the meeting.
The Malaysian minister arrived in Lima earlier on Thursday on a "special mission" for the "safe and early release" of the ambassador, according to the Foreign Ministry in Kuala Lumpur.
Ahmad Mokhtar was one of five ambassadors left in the residence after the release of Guatemalan Ambassador Jose Maria Argueta on Thursday and Uruguayan Ambassador Tabare Bocalandro on Wednesday.
Argueta said his release was an "acknowledgement" by the MRTA of his country's peace process with leftist rebels. Bocalandro was freed after the release from jail in Montevideo of two MRTA suspects.
